key_insight: RubriQ turns quantum circuit synthesis into an LLM-based code-generation problem and improves it with rubric-guided GRPO to produce more efficient, hardware-compatible circuits.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides an HPC-scalable path to automated fault-tolerant circuit generation, helping bridge the gap between theoretical quantum algorithms and deployable hardware-ready implementations.
method: Uses a domain-grounded rubric as the RL reward, scoring T-gate reduction, topology compliance, and unitary fidelity.
Trains an LLM with group relative policy optimization (GRPO) instead of a black-box neural critic.
Integrates GPU-accelerated CUDA-Q simulation and multi-node DeepSpeed ZeRO2 on Perlmutter for fast RL training.
evidence_signal: On benchmark tasks, RubriQ achieves 3.31x mean T-gate compression versus 2.05x for sparse-reward RL, converges 2–3x faster, and keeps hardware-constraint violations below 1%, with validation on IBM and IonQ devices.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and completeness of the rubric and simulation-to-hardware transfer may still introduce mismatch or scaling challenges on larger circuits.
paper_title: RubriQ: Rubric-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization for Constraint-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
